For a rocky planet, the radius does not scale linearly with mass because internal compression makes larger planets comparatively smaller in radius than a simple M ∝ R³ scaling would suggest. A commonly–used empirical mass-radius relation for rocky (Earth-like composition) planets is  

  R ∝ M^0.27   (for roughly 0.1–10 M⊕).

Density ρ = M / (4⁄3 πR³) ∝ M / R³ ⇒ ρ ∝ M / (M^0.27)³ = M / M^0.81 = M^0.19.

So, relative to Earth (M = 1, ρ = ρ⊕ ≈ 5.5 g cm⁻³):

• Case (c): M = 5 M⊕ → ρ ≈ ρ⊕ × 5^0.19 ≈ 5.5 g cm⁻³ × 1.35 ≈ 7.4 g cm⁻³.  
• Case (d): M = 0.5 M⊕ → ρ ≈ ρ⊕ × 0.5^0.19 ≈ 5.5 g cm⁻³ × 0.88 ≈ 4.8 g cm⁻³.  
• Case (a): ρ = 5.5 g cm⁻³ (by definition of Earth).  
• Case (b): ρ is explicitly stated as 5.5 g cm⁻³.

Therefore the highest density is for the 5-Earth-mass rocky planet in option (c).

Letter mapping: (A) corresponds to c.

Answer: A
